Summary: The DRAGIN framework consists of two components: Real-time Information Needs Detection (RIND) and Query Formulation based on Self-attention (QFS). RIND determines the optimal moment for activation of the retrieval module by assessing the LLM's uncertainty, the importance of each token, and the semantic significance within the generated content. QFS crafts retrieval queries leveraging the LLM's self-attention mechanism for a comprehensive understanding of the context. The framework is designed to dynamically decide when and what to retrieve based on the LLM’s real-time information needs, significantly improving the relevance and accuracy of generated text. It is lightweight and can be seamlessly integrated into any Transformer-based LLM without additional training or fine-tuning. However, the method relies on the self-attention mechanism of Transformer-based LLMs and is not applicable to certain APIs that do not provide access to self-attention scores.
